name: What is a bump-out addition and how does it differ from a full room addition?

mainEntity.name: What is a bump-out addition and how does it differ from a full room addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A bump-out addition is an extension of an existing room that expands the footprint of your home by a small margin, typically a few feet. Unlike a full room addition, a bump-out usually does not require a new foundation. It often cantilevers beyond the existing foundation or uses a simpler, localized foundation. This approach is ideal for homeowners seeking to add space, such as expanding a kitchen for an island, creating a larger dining nook, or adding depth to a bedroom, without the extensive structural and foundational work of a complete new room. AKN Design Group specializes in ensuring these smaller additions seamlessly integrate with your existing home's structure and aesthetics.
acceptedAnswer.description: A bump-out addition expands an existing room by a few feet, often without needing a full new foundation, unlike a larger room addition.
